\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{स्थिति} (sthiti)}{स्थिति (sthiti)}]{\hi{स्थिति} (sthiti) — a situation}

\label{lesson:HI-C377-sthiti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for bound to happen, then the Hindi for to emerge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{स्थिति}}
\textbf{\hi{स्थिति}} — \emph{sthiti} — \textquotedblleft{}a situation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{स्थिति} \hi{बिगड़ेगी} \hi{तो} \hi{हम} \hi{शहर} \hi{छोड़} \hi{देंगे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sthiti bigṛegī to ham śahar choṛ deṅge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the situation gets worse, we'll leave the city.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{स्थिति}} (\emph{sthiti}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{sthiti}, \textquotedblleft{}standing, a state\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthiti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthiti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar sthiti bigṛegī to ham śahar choṛ deṅge.} — If the situation gets worse, we'll leave the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for bound to happen, then the Hindi for to emerge, then say \emph{sthiti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{स्थिति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A situation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हालत} (hālat)}{हालत (hālat)}]{\hi{हालत} (hālat) — a state (of health, repair), a condition}

\label{lesson:HI-C377-halat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to emerge, then the Hindi for a situation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हालत}}
\textbf{\hi{हालत}} — \emph{hālat} — \textquotedblleft{}a state (of health, repair), a condition\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{गाड़ी} \hi{की} \hi{हालत} \hi{ठीक} \hi{होती} \hi{तो} \hi{हम} \hi{आज} \hi{निकलते।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar gāṛī kī hālat ṭhīk hotī to ham āj nikalte.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the car were in good condition, we'd set off today.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हालत}} (\emph{hālat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḥāla}, \textquotedblleft{}a state, a condition\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hālat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar gāṛī kī hālat ṭhīk hotī to ham āj nikalte.} — If the car were in good condition, we'd set off today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to emerge, then the Hindi for a situation, then say \emph{hālat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ज़रूरत} (zarūrat)}{ज़रूरत (zarūrat)}]{\hi{ज़रूरत} (zarūrat) — a need}

\label{lesson:HI-C377-zarurat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a situation, then the Hindi for a state (of health, repair).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ज़रूरत}}
\textbf{\hi{ज़रूरत}} — \emph{zarūrat} — \textquotedblleft{}a need\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम्हें} \hi{पैसों} \hi{की} \hi{ज़रूरत} \hi{होगी} \hi{तो} \hi{मुझे} \hi{बताओ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tumhẽ paisoṁ kī zarūrat hogī to mujhe batāo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you need money, tell me.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ज़रूरत}} (\emph{zarūrat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḍarūra}, \textquotedblleft{}necessity\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{मुसीबत} (musībat)}{मुसीबत (musībat)}]{\hi{मुसीबत} (musībat) — a hardship, trouble}

\label{lesson:HI-C377-musibat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a state (of health, repair), then the Hindi for a need.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{मुसीबत}}
\textbf{\hi{मुसीबत}} — \emph{musībat} — \textquotedblleft{}a hardship, trouble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{झूठ} \hi{बोलोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{मुसीबत} \hi{में} \hi{पड़ोगे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum jhūṭh bologe to musībat meṁ paṛoge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you lie, you'll land in trouble.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{मुसीबत}} (\emph{musībat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{muṣība}, \textquotedblleft{}a misfortune\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{फँसाना} (phãsānā)}{फँसाना (phãsānā)}]{\hi{फँसाना} (phãsānā) — to trap, to land (someone) in trouble}

\label{lesson:HI-C377-phasana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a need, then the Hindi for a hardship.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{फँसाना}}
\textbf{\hi{फँसाना}} — \emph{phãsānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to trap, to land (someone) in trouble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{उस} \hi{आदमी} \hi{की} \hi{बात} \hi{मानोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{वह} \hi{तुम्हें} \hi{फँसा} \hi{देगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum us ādmī kī bāt mānoge to vah tumhẽ phãsā degā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you listen to that man, he'll land you in trouble.
\end{quote}

Past, with \hi{ने} (he or she …): \hi{उसने} \hi{मुझे} \hi{फँसाया}, \emph{usne mujhe phãsāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{फँसाना}} (\emph{phãsānā}) is a tadbhava, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{spāśayati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to be bound\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13814).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a need, then the Hindi for a hardship, then say \emph{phãsānā} again
\end{itemize}
